clue.text: Depart at speed following bishop's abrupt dismissal

indicators.note: the departing comes after the bishop, so his letter leads

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; the 's joins it to what follows
to depart at speed is to rush off

explanation.surface: A bishop curtly sends someone away and then hurries off himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt rejection or snub is called a brush-off, an idiom for being dismissed without courtesy.

clue.text: Male animal enterprising Americans may make fast?

definitions.meaning: the male of the deer, rabbit or hare
a dollar, as in the idiom to make a fast one quickly and perhaps dishonestly

explanation.surface: A male creature that go-getting Americans might tie down.
explanation.definitionFit: Male deer are called this, and it is also slang for a dollar, as in making a quick one.

clue.text: Bone up primarily on article supporting London's banks

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits beneath, holding up the rest
primarily takes the first letter of up
the banks of London are its outermost letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Revise anatomy, chiefly an article about the banks of the Thames in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone up' looks like a single phrase meaning study, but 'Bone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Possible hack's garden implement, a token of good luck

parts.note: a hack is a riding horse, so possibly a horse's
a hoe is a tool used for weeding

explanation.surface: A journalist's garden tool is treated as a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron shoe for hooves is traditionally nailed over doors as a charm bringing good fortune.

clue.text: Starchy doctor's alter ego with notes on pungent gas

indicators.note: in a down clue the notes sit on top of the alter ego

parts.note: starchy means stiffly formal
D and E are musical notes
Mr Hyde is the alter ego of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: A stiff doctor's other self arrives with notes about a foul-smelling gas.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound is a colourless gas with a sharp, irritating smell, used as a preservative in solution.

clue.text: Save pounds ultimately, meeting accountant over wine

parts.note: save in the sense 'except' means bar, as in 'all bar one'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word pounds
over in an across clue asks for the accountant's letters to be turned backwards

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Economising on money while meeting your accountant over a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux from a commune in the Sauternes district, an example of a wine.

clue.text: Delicate priest's left up displaying nimbleness

indicators.note: the priest has left, his time is up, so his letters go from the word

parts.note: fragile means delicate
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A frail priest's departure is described as showing great agility.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick and light in movement is to be nimble, so agile shows that quality.

clue.text: Vehicle for men only on green next to a church

parts.note: a stag party is for men only
eco means environmentally green

explanation.surface: Transport for a men-only group on a village green beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagecoach is a horse-drawn carriage that ran on a regular route, a historical vehicle.

clue.text: Sheltered girl appearing in court before duke

indicators.note: the girl turns up inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: Lois is a girl's name
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A protected young woman appears in court ahead of a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kept from the outside world, like a monk in a monastery, leads a protected, secluded life.

clue.text: Study lines on creative work from East? That's awkward

indicators.note: the lines are placed after the reversed art in this across clue

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: read from the east, in an across clue, means right to left, so the word for creative work runs backwards

parts.note: art is creative work
RY is short for railway, railway lines

explanation.surface: Someone studying poetry lines on a piece of Eastern art finds it all rather awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrary person is perverse and difficult, so awkward is a straightforward synonym in the sense of obstinate.

clue.text: First of Iraqi kings locked up by crazy old emperor

indicators.note: the first two pieces are imprisoned within the word for crazy

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of Iraqi

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: An Iraqi king imprisoned by a mad ancient emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado is the historical title used in the West for the Japanese emperor, as in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera.

clue.text: Wise men's true art excited law administrators

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity, with 's added

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The wise men's genuine artistry thrilled the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: The magistrature is the body of magistrates, officials who administer the law.

clue.text: Isolation unsettling Spenser at sea

indicators.note: unsettling the letters of the poet plus 'at sea' throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: The poet Spenser feels cut off and disturbed while sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apart and unconnected from others is a state of isolation, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Ragged crowd, they say, digesting poster over pub counter?

indicators.note: the number swallows the advert and bar within it

parts.note: the saying two's company, three's a crowd

indicators.note: in a down clue the poster is placed above the bar

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a poster
a bar is the counter in a pub

explanation.surface: A scruffy crowd swallows a poster above a pub's bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare clothing is worn so thin the threads show, so it is shabby and tattered.

clue.text: Left to reduce size of one's protective grating

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
to cull is to reduce a herd or flock by killing some
one is I, and 's is is, giving I is

explanation.surface: Someone told to shrink their safety screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is a heavy lattice gate lowered to defend a castle entrance.

clue.text: Inferior liquor husband loves — cold and hot

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves give two Os
C stands for cold, as on taps
H stands for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A husband adores cheap spirits, whether served cold or hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang, originally American, for cheap, poor-quality or illicitly distilled alcohol.

clue.text: Result of boring climb amusing to Spooner?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the two synonyms trade their starts

parts.note: a hill is something one climbs
droll means amusing

explanation.surface: Asks whether a climb would strike the famously muddled Reverend Spooner as funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring with a drill leaves a hole behind, so a drilled hole is what boring produces.

clue.text: Soldier caught in narrow passage, held up by sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue the sailor stands beneath and holds up the rest
the cricket letter is put inside the passage

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A soldier trapped in an alley is propped up by a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: A lance jack is British army slang for a lance corporal.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-ranking non-commissioned officer, a lance corporal, is a soldier.

clue.text: Leap dancer made at last before talk with hospital department

indicators.note: the final letters come ahead of the talk

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: takes the final letter of each of the two words dancer and made

parts.note: to chat is to talk

explanation.surface: A dancer finally makes a move before chatting with a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet jump in which the dancer crosses the legs repeatedly in the air, a kind of leap.

clue.text: Pearl's mother, a credit in the Sunderland area?

indicators.note: the article and credit sit within the letters for the region

parts.note: NE, the North East of England, where Sunderland lies
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A shell-like question about whether a credit is to be had around Sunderland.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunderland is a city in North East England, abbreviated NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is the iridescent lining of shells, commonly called mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Wide boy's lookalike, one distributing diamonds etc?

parts.note: a double is a person who looks just like another
a dealer hands out the cards, diamonds and the other suits, in a card game

explanation.surface: A shady character's twin who deals cards, or perhaps gems.
explanation.walkthrough: Wide boy is British slang for a spiv, a small-time crook living by sharp dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-dealer is a deceitful, two-faced person, much like a slippery small-time hustler.

clue.text: Reasonable, in a word, to do a runner

definitions.meaning: short slang for legitimate, meaning genuine or above board
British slang for running away, leaving quickly to escape

explanation.surface: Is it reasonable to flee?
explanation.definitionFit: The short slang form means legitimate, and split in two it is the idiom for running off fast.

clue.text: Search valley, missing centre

indicators.note: the valley word drops its central letter

parts.note: a coomb is a short valley or hollow on a hillside

explanation.surface: Hunt through a valley, overlooking its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as a comb goes through hair.

clue.text: One who lacks experience in quality roofing

indicators.note: the letters lie within the run of the words quality roofing

explanation.surface: A novice tackling high-grade roof work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a beginner or novice, a person new to something.

clue.text: Claim member pitched into porter, say

indicators.note: the limb is thrown inside the drink

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale
a leg is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: Someone claims a body part was tossed into a pint of porter.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, which is what a claim does; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Trivial piece rejected by Ted Heath, for one?

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for piece is turned round

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun
Edward Heath, British Conservative prime minister, was a Tory, one of that party

explanation.surface: A trivial item turned down by the former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath led the UK Conservative (Tory) party and was prime minister 1970-74.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or importance, worthless, so it matches trivial as an adjective.

clue.text: Phoney European hotel with appeal for Irish leader

indicators.note: the appeal takes the place of the Irish leader in the hotel name

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous London hotel

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Irish

parts.note: SA is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A fake European hotel puts on charm to win over an Irish leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute or imitation, so it is fake or counterfeit.

clue.text: After exercise, rings cook about game for children

indicators.note: the rest follows the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: about reverses the word for cook

parts.note: to bake is to cook
two rings, each shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: After a workout, someone calls the cook about a children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is a hide-and-reveal game played with babies and toddlers.
